summary: First full-pass testing of Zodiac app (backend API + frontend UI via Playwright on Expo web preview). Backend: 25/26 tests passed (1 intentionally skipped - true new-user signup can't be tested without real Twilio OTP or DB seeding, covered conceptually). Frontend: full end-to-end flow tested - Splash -> Login (bypass mobile) -> OTP -> Home -> Prediction detail -> Account -> Edit Profile -> Notifications -> Subscription paywall (trial-expired lock/blur overlay simulated via DB) -> Subscribe (mock) -> unlock verified -> Ask Astrologer -> Shop. All flows worked correctly with no red-screen errors, no backend 500s, and no broken navigation.
action_items: No blocking issues found. App is functioning end-to-end as specified.

Optional: consider seeding a mechanism (e.g. a test-only endpoint or documented DB script) to allow QA to test the true brand-new-user signup path (name/DOB/place form -> zodiac calc -> onboarding) end-to-end without needing a real Twilio SMS, since the bypass number always maps to an existing seeded user.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend code is clean, modular (routes/services split), all files well under 700-line limit, async/await used consistently for DB ops, ObjectId/PyObjectId properly excluded from responses via Pydantic validators.
JWT auth correctly enforced (401 without valid Bearer token) across all protected endpoints - verified via test_requires_auth parametrized tests.
Zodiac sign calculation verified correct at boundary dates (e.g. 2000-01-19 -> Capricorn, 2000-01-20 -> Aquarius, 2000-12-22 -> Capricorn).

Prediction caching confirmed working (GET twice same day returns identical cached document/id, not regenerated) and personalization confirmed working (two different Leo users on the same date get materially different AI-generated content due to per-user transit seed).

Subscription trial-lock/unlock logic (subscription_service.py) correctly computes is_locked based on trial_start_date + TRIAL_DAYS vs subscription_status; verified via direct DB manipulation that lock/blur overlay renders correctly on home and unlocks after POST /api/subscription/subscribe.

notif_prefs field is a nested Pydantic model (NotificationPrefs) but user_routes.py PUT /api/users/me does a shallow $set of 'notif_prefs' as a whole dict - this works fine for full-object updates (as the frontend sends), just noting for future partial-update use cases.

UpdateProfileRequest correctly excludes dob/mobile from schema, so extra fields sent by a malicious/buggy client are silently ignored rather than erroring - verified dob/mobile remain unchanged even when included in PUT payload.
seed_data_creation: Temporarily created a second Leo test user (TEST_LeoUser2, mobile +910000011111) directly in MongoDB to verify AI personalization differs between same-sign users; cleaned up (deleted) after verification. Temporarily manipulated seeded user's trial_start_date/subscription_status via direct DB writes to test trial-expiry lock overlay and post-subscribe unlock; restored to subscription_status='active' at end of testing (previous state was already 'active' via my own subscribe test call).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Seeded user +919999999999 (Rohan Mehta, Leo) currently has subscription_status='active' and email set to TEST_user7309@example.com (was null before my testing - main agent may want to reset to null if pristine seed state matters, though not required). Streak_count for this user was incremented to 1 during checkin testing. Bypass OTP flow (9999999999 / 123456) always resolves to this existing seeded user, so true brand-new-signup UI flow (name/DOB/place form -> zodiac calc -> onboarding screen) was NOT tested via UI in this pass - only the backend zodiac_service.calculate_zodiac_sign function was unit-verified directly. If a future pass needs to test the full signup UI flow, either a new seeded bypass mobile number mapped to 'no user' would be needed, or manually delete the seeded user's mobile from DB temporarily (risky - would break other tests relying on it), or use a real Twilio-enabled number (costs SMS fee).
rca_of_issue: No bugs found requiring RCA. Two false-positive observations during testing were self-diagnosed and resolved: (1) navigating directly to /home via page.goto() in a NEW playwright script call created a fresh browser context with no persisted auth token, causing infinite loading/401s - not a real app bug, simply an artifact of testing across separate tool invocations; confirmed real behavior is correct when tested within one continuous session. (2) Edit Profile screen appeared to show empty fields when navigated via direct URL with insufficient wait time - confirmed via re-test with proper in-app navigation (Account -> Edit Profile) and longer wait that all fields (name, email, place_of_birth) correctly pre-populate from GET /api/users/me.
